hook_text: Under the dry ground of a village in North West, there is water hiding in the rocks, nearly a hundred metres down.
clip_script: A big truck with a tall drilling tower rumbles into a village near Mahikeng. The drill spins, roaring and dusty, going deeper and deeper into the rock, day after day. Then, at about ninety metres, water gushes up, muddy at first, then clear. A pump is lowered into the hole, solar panels are set up, and soon water flows into a tank and out of taps for the whole village. Water from deep underground.
visual_style: Whiteboard cross-section: a wide hand-dug well with a bucket and rope, and next to it a narrow borehole drilled deep into rock layers to an aquifer, with a pump, solar panel, tank and taps above.
mood: Exciting and hopeful, like waiting for a surprise.
pacing: Slow, noisy drilling build-up, then a burst of joy when the water comes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look out for windmills, hand pumps or borehole tanks near you.
